scenario.name: NSA/CISA Kubernetes Guide & CNCF Falco DFIR — Kubernetes Audit Log Privileged Pod & hostPath Container Escape
scenario.overview: Picture a brick university lecture and exam hall with tiered wooden student desks, a tall green chalkboard, hallway lockers, and a wooden proctor podium at the front. Inside the quiet university exam hall, a student slips hidden extra directions written in faint pencil into the margin of a submitted study booklet. In this real-world scenario, the intruder leaves a hidden spare latch behind so they can walk back into the university hall later, then smuggles copied records out past the lecture hall attendance desk in tiny disguised batches. The university dean reviews the exam hall proctor log and flags an automated grading run that tried to access locked answer folders mid-session. In this scenario (T1613, NSA/CISA Kubernetes Guide & CNCF Falco DFIR, Kubernetes Audit Log Privileged Pod & hostPath Container Escape), the attacker follows one continuous intrusion path so each later Step can show the exact handoff that makes the next stage possible. The attack unfolds in one continuous arc: serviceAccount RBAC SelfSubjectRulesReview, then privileged Pod Creation with hostPID: true, then host Namespace Escape via nsenter -t 1 -m -u. Steps #1–#3 walk that chain end-to-end by covering ServiceAccount RBAC SelfSubjectRulesReview, then Privileged Pod Creation with hostPID: true, then Host Namespace Escape via nsenter -t 1 -m -u, while the Process Hierarchy tab keeps the Parent → Child spawn tree visible so you can see which trusted process launched the next payload. Primary detection pivots on Auditd Event 201 correlated across the documented kill chain.
